glossary.definition: An AI agent that acts for a customer: it asks for a list of trips, a flight booking, a flight status. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

RFC 8693 token exchange mints a delegated token whose sub is the customer and whose act claim names the agent. Delegation, not impersonation. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.
The customer lets a named agent act for them before the exchange. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

A permitted call whose arguments the rule narrows (here the cabin, business to economy). The outcome word CONSTRAINED is the lab's own. With the PingOne Authorize settings set, PingOne Authorize decides the booking and the lab applies its answer; otherwise the lab's fare rule decides it, and the page says it is not a PingOne Authorize outcome. The two fare limits and the international flag are lab-invented. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

A policy decision on every call: PERMIT, DENY, or an obligation (step-up, human approval, CIBA). The airline pack adds one outcome of the lab's own, CONSTRAINED. The lab's thresholds are lab-invented, fitted to the catalog's example amounts. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

A risky write returns an obligation instead of running: a second factor first, or a verified human approval receipt. A boolean "approved" flag from the client does not count. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

The agent asks the identity provider to authenticate the customer on another device and polls until they approve. Needs a feature flag; the lab runs it on its own steps here. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

The gateway validates signature, audience, expiry, act claim and scope, applies rate limits and edge policy, and fails closed. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

A nested act claim when one agent hands work to another: scope is narrowed at each hop and an unregistered agent in the chain is denied. The use case is from the AI-DEMO2 catalog; the amounts and events are lab-invented.

On this path (the owner's opt-in) a run makes two real calls to one PingOne environment: its discovery document and the agent's own client-credentials token (shown masked). It runs nothing else: no customer sign-in, token exchange, gateway check, policy decision or tool call, and it lists the steps it did not run. The path has not been run against a real tenant by the builder: UNVERIFIED.
Tokens in this lab are issued by the lab and signed ES256 with a public key. They protect nothing and are shown raw for education.

cards.label: Run delegated access (UC1)
cards.description: Sign in as the demo customer, consent, exchange, gateway check, authorize, dispatch: seven hops, each with its raw request and response.

cards.label: Run the international booking next to the domestic one
cards.description: Run the international booking next to the domestic one: same fare, the second is booked in economy. The agent asked for business and the answer says what was narrowed. The limits and the flag are lab-invented.

cards.label: Run the booking over the higher limit
cards.description: A booking over the second limit returns an approval obligation and the write is held until a person approves. Thresholds are lab-invented.

cards.label: Run the DPoP replay attack (UC12)
cards.description: The first proof is accepted and the replay is refused with 401. Needs the feature ff_dpop; the lab runs it on its own steps here.

cards.label: Why it matters: a customer-facing agent that cannot overreach
cards.description: Challenge: Appfire's HIVE platform already manages the backend: data policy and which MCP servers may be used. The open question is the agent-facing front end: who or what the agent is, what it is allowed to do, under which conditions, and how each decision is enforced and recorded — without a person approving every step. Technical: Ping governs the front end: the agent gets its own identity, receives delegated privileges (RFC 8693 act chain), and every tool call, MCP-server hop and data access gets a policy decision with a risk-based outcome — auto-allow for low-risk reads, step-up or human approval for risky writes, deny for out-of-scope actions — all enforced at the tool, data and action layers, not left to the model. Business: Controlled autonomy: low-risk actions proceed inside policy, higher-risk ones are constrained or approved, and every decision leaves an audit record naming the agent, the principal it acted for, the resource and the decision — the visibility Appfire's AI Governance program is asking for, complementing (not replacing) HIVE. (Lab summary of the AI-DEMO2 catalog text, not a Ping claim.)

cards.label: The identity-provider-only path
cards.description: It reaches the identity provider only and lists what it did not run. UNVERIFIED on a real tenant.

cards.label: Lab-issued tokens
cards.description: Every token is signed with a public key and shown raw with its decoded claims.

cards.label: Doctor and health
cards.description: Preflight checks and the demo-health/1 endpoint.
